brief:
Far-right Israeli Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir entered the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound accompanied by settlers, according to Al Jazeera English. The visit marked a breach of a longstanding arrangement that has governed access to the sacred site for decades, with protocols restricting Israeli officials and Jewish visitors' presence at the location.

The status quo arrangement has remained largely intact since Israel's 1967 occupation of East Jerusalem, where the mosque compound sits atop the Temple Mount. Ben-Gvir's entry with settlers represents a significant departure from the informal understandings that have historically limited such visits by Israeli government figures and Jewish groups to the contested religious site.
dek: Israeli Minister Ben-Gvir storms Al-Aqsa Mosque compound with settlers, violating decades-old status quo arrangement.
title: Ben-Gvir storms Al-Aqsa Mosque compound alongside settlers
